title: Annotatio IV §.XX: (2–3) Silence spiritual-mode half; Strauch despairs — organ of eating usually named Faith
pass_a_gloss: (2) About to introduce that part of the Waldenses’ Confession by which they profess the presence of Christ’s Body in the Supper — admitted by the Reformed no less than by Lutherans — yet Danhauer §. 31 and Strauch in the cited aphorism in the ekthesis §. 1 wrap in deep silence the other part of the Confession, by which everywhere they proclaim the mode of this presence Spiritual, opposed to the corporal. (3) About to expound from the Waldenses’ mind the organ of eating Christ’s body, Strauch plainly despairs of the Waldenses’ Consensus with the Lutherans, writing thus in §. 2: But for the rest, since in other Waldensian Confessions the doctrine of the sacraments is expounded rather obscurely, and the organ of participating in the heavenly thing is most often named FAITH, let others’ judgment be concerning the Orthodoxy of the Neoteric Waldenses, and especially of those who implore the Calvinists’ protection, &c. &c.
pass_b_english: (2) Danhauer and Strauch parade the confession’s presence half (admitted by Reformed and Lutheran alike) but wrap in deep silence the half that everywhere preaches the mode as Spiritual, opposed to corporal.

(3) On the organ of eating, Strauch plainly despairs of Lutheran consensus — other confessions obscurely name FAITH as the organ of sharing the heavenly thing; let others judge neoteric Waldenses who seek Calvinist protection.
source_text: (2) Introductura eam Confessionis Waldensium partem, quâ Corporis Christi in Cœna præsentiam isti profitentur, à Reformatis non minùs quàm Lutheranis admissam, alteram tamen Confessionis partem, quâ præsentiæ hujus modum ubique deprædicant Spiritualem, corporali oppositum, alto silentio involvit Danhauerus §. 31. & Strauchius cit. aphorism. in ekthesei §. 1. (3) Organon manducationis corporis Christi ex mente Waldensium expositurus Strauchius, de Waldensium cum Lutheranis Consensu planè desperat, ita §. 2. scribens: Cæterùm cum in aliis Waldensium Confessionibus obscuriuscule exponatur sacramentorum doctrina, & organon participandi rei cælestis plerumque FIDES nominetur, aliorum sit de Orthodoxia Waldensium Neotericorum, & imprimis eorum qui Calvinianorum tutelam implorant, judicium &c. &c.
notes: (2–3) Silence spiritual mode; faith as organ.
